deals.evidence: Mr Justice Fancourt ruled Mr McCabe must now sell his stake to Prince Abdullah for £5m.
deals.headline: High Court orders McCabe to sell his 50% of Sheffield United to Prince Abdullah for £5m
deals.investor: UTB LLC (Prince Abdullah bin Mosaad bin Abdulaziz Al Saud)
deals.summary: Ending the 50-50 ownership dispute, the High Court ruled Kevin McCabe's Sheffield United Ltd must sell its stake to Prince Abdullah's UTB LLC for £5m; UTB also had to buy the club's property assets, including Bramall Lane.

deals.evidence: The takeover of Sheffield United has been officially completed by American-based consortium COH Sports.
deals.headline: COH Sports completes takeover of Sheffield United
deals.investor: COH Sports (COH Sports Bidco Limited; Steven Rosen and Helmy Eltoukhy)
deals.seller: United World (Prince Abdullah bin Mosaad Al Saud)
deals.summary: American consortium COH Sports, led by Steven Rosen and Helmy Eltoukhy, completed the purchase of 100% of the club, the women's team, the Bramall Lane hotel and all real estate. The BBC later reported the agreed price as 'just over £100m', paid partly in instalments, of which about £35m remained unpaid in 2026.

deals.evidence: Msd Investment Corp. as Security Agent
deals.headline: MSD Investment Corp. takes security over Sheffield United's assets
deals.summary: A charge created on 14 January 2026 in favour of MSD Investment Corp. as security agent, including fixed security over land, was registered against The Sheffield United Football Club Limited (a matching charge was registered against Blades Leisure Limited). The loan amount is not disclosed on the register.

deals.evidence: United’s borrowing obligations include a £24m bank loan secured against future Premier League income
deals.headline: £24m Macquarie bank loan secured against future Premier League income
deals.summary: The club's accounts to June 2025 show a £24m bank loan secured against future Premier League income plus factoring of transfer receivables; Macquarie Bank's London branch holds several outstanding charges over the club.

deals.evidence: In June, the shares in the club were transferred from CSBL into a new US-based company - 1919 Partners LLC
deals.headline: Club shares moved from COH Sports Bidco to new Delaware parent 1919 Partners LLC
deals.summary: In June 2026 the shares in the club were transferred from COH Sports Bidco Limited into 1919 Partners LLC, a US company controlled by Rosen and Eltoukhy. COH Sports Bidco was then wound up by the High Court on 19 August 2026 on United World's petition over about £35m of unpaid purchase price.

founded_evidence: Sheffield United, known as the Blades, was founded in 1889
name: Sheffield United Football Club
notes: Revenue is the club company's turnover (£79.3m, 2024-25); the holding company Blades Leisure Limited's consolidated turnover, which includes the DoubleTree hotel, was £82,596,849 with a £17.6m operating loss and £1,809,474 profit before tax (group accounts to 30 June 2025, a scanned PDF at Companies House, read by OCR, so not used as evidence). Stakes: Companies House only gives the band 'more than 25% but not more than 50%' for each of Rosen and Eltoukhy, so stake_pct is null. The purchase price is only stated as 'just over £100m' (BBC), so no amount or valuation is recorded. The MSD loan amount is not public. A Santander UK charge (28 April 2026) is also on the register. No Forbes/Sportico valuation exists for the club. The EFL and IFR were considering action over the June 2026 share transfer at the time of writing; a points deduction was possible. Wages, attendance, shirt sponsor, kit supplier and social counts not found on citable pages; the club's own site (sufc.co.uk) renders client-side and could not be read.

ownership_summary: Controlled by US businessmen Steven Rosen (founder of Resilience Capital Partners) and Helmy Eltoukhy (chair of Guardant Health), co-chairmen, who bought 100% from Prince Abdullah bin Mosaad's United World in December 2024 through COH Sports Bidco Limited. In June 2026 the shares were moved to a new Delaware parent, 1919 Partners LLC; Companies House lists Rosen and Eltoukhy each with more than 25% but not more than 50% of the holding company Blades Leisure Limited from 28 May 2026. COH Sports Bidco was wound up by the High Court on 19 August 2026 with about £35m of the purchase price unpaid.
